title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM filter() with keyword arguments constructed via dictionary unpacking. The provider_type._meta.model_name is a model metadata attribute (not user input), and the f-string construction is safe for ORM usage. No raw SQL or string concatenation into SQL queries is present.
No SQL queries are modified in this file. The changes involve viewset mixins and field serialization only.
No SQL injection vectors in this file. The changes involve HTTP request handling, headers construction, and database model operations via Django ORM (which use parameterized queries).

The SSFStreamViewSet was changed from ReadOnlyModelViewSet to explicit mixins including DestroyModelMixin. This adds DELETE capability to the viewset. The diff does not show the complete permission_classes or has_permission/has_object_permission implementations. Without seeing authorization checks in the viewset, it's unclear if DELETE operations are properly protected. This could allow unauthorized deletion of Stream objects.

evidence.content:
-class SSFStreamViewSet(ReadOnlyModelViewSet):
+class SSFStreamViewSet(
+    mixins.RetrieveModelMixin,
+    mixins.DestroyModelMixin,
+    mixins.ListModelMixin,
+    GenericViewSet,
+):
     """SSFStream Viewset"""

     queryset = Stream.objects.all()

findings.suggested_fix: Verify that SSFStreamViewSet has appropriate permission_classes (e.g., IsAuthenticated, custom ownership checks) and has_object_permission() method to ensure only authorized users can delete Stream objects. Consider implementing object-level authorization to verify the user owns or has access to the stream being deleted.

findings.explanation: The SSFStreamViewSet uses queryset = Stream.objects.all(), which retrieves all Stream objects without filtering by ownership or authorization. Combined with the new DestroyModelMixin, this could allow users to access/delete streams they don't own. However, without seeing the complete viewset implementation (permission_classes, get_queryset override), we cannot confirm if authorization checks exist elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Override get_queryset() to filter streams by the authenticated user's accessible providers, or implement has_object_permission() to verify authorization before allowing retrieve/destroy operations on individual Stream objects.
